cells.tense: Holding power is flowing out to the people around you right now, and you are choosing what to put where.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that's already flowing and decide today how much goes where. Choose the amount before the next ask lands.
cells.core:
You're carrying weight and handing some of it out on purpose. Not dumping it, not keeping all of it against a bad year — you know what people around you can hold right now, and you've been matching that with what you've got.

Good looks like this: something you built to last is now steadying somebody else, and you can say so without making it a debt. What's coming in just now is a request or an opening — a thing arriving that could take more of you than it needs. Look at the size of it before you answer. Staying balanced costs something: it asks you to name the measure out loud instead of quietly erring generous.
cells.sheetLine: You're sharing real strength by measure, and choosing the measure.
cells.place: the doorway where what is outside comes in

cells.tense: You are already spending strength on needs that have not arrived yet and may not be yours to carry.
cells.ask: Say no this week to one need nobody has actually put to you. Let one thing stay unhandled for a day.
cells.core:
You're out ahead of what's coming, holding weight for people who haven't asked. There's a load you're braced under right now that no one has handed you — a worry you've decided you'll be carrying, an arrangement made in your head for a need that might not land.

When holding works, it contains without crushing — it stays the size of what's actually there. What's bending it now is that you've taken the shape of every possible need ahead of time, and the strength meant for the real thing is going into rehearsal. Fairness isn't a calculation you run in advance. Put one of those loads down and see that nothing you carry for real falls with it.
cells.sheetLine: You're footing bills nobody handed you yet.

cells.tense: You were in a place where your strength had somewhere to go, and you are still standing back from the door.
cells.ask: Give one concrete thing to one person this week — an hour, a ride, a hand with something. Small, direct, done.
cells.core:
You've got strength that used to move out to people, and it isn't moving. The standing-back is the thing to look at — you can feel the door there and you're not walking through it. The strength hasn't gone anywhere. The handing-over stopped.

What it looks like when this is working: strength that moves outward by measure, holding without forcing. What's starved isn't the strength, it's the way out, and pushing feeling or effort straight at the still part won't fill it. Start with a thing you can actually give — finished, real, small enough to complete — and let that be the test. What you let go of when something is done isn't loss. It's the thing finally working.
cells.sheetLine: You have strength to share and you've stopped handing it over.

cells.tense: Strength is already moving from you out to the people around you while you describe it as just what the situation needs.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're already providing and say out loud that it's yours to provide. One sentence, to someone.
cells.core:
People are steady because of something you do, and you've been talking about it like it just happens. The support is running — you're carrying it out to others — and you haven't put your name on it. You file it under practical, under how it has to go.

Good looks like this: strength that moves outward because what you built reached the point of being able to hold someone else. The offering is yours. What's missing is the saying-so — the one sentence that puts you in the sentence you're already living out. That sentence is simpler than it feels. What you're doing is real. Only the credit is absent.
cells.sheetLine: You're already supporting people. You haven't put your name on it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is authorship in the Unacknowledged cell: I can describe a mechanism running without a claim on it, but I cannot say the person 'built' anything in the Support line, and I won't. A reader could reasonably say the arriving thing is simply other people's need landing on them, not strength of their own moving outward — the cards don't settle whose it is, so the cell only names the shape of what's coming in. If I'm wrong about the direction of the flow, the ask still works: naming one concrete thing already in motion is useful whether it started with them or arrived from elsewhere. The sentence that would serve me rather than them is any form of 'this is what's really happening to you' — cut on sight.
